data.why: the sidebar 'Try an example' menu generates eight simulated diffraction patterns (rings, spots, amorphous) with known ground-truth answers directly in app.py/saedscope/synth.py, so no uploaded files are needed to exercise the full workflow

goals: identify the phase and zone axis that explain a single-crystal spot pattern
identify the phase(s) producing a polycrystalline ring pattern, including a possible second phase
check whether a scale bar or nominal calibration is consistent with the candidate phase, and by how much it would need to be off
test a pattern against my own CIF file(s) and see which structures are consistent, partly consistent, or not consistent
get the next specimen tilt that would distinguish between two competing phase/zone-axis answers
estimate the nearest-neighbour distance of an amorphous halo

review.summary: The tree accurately covers SAEDscope's demo path (ring, spot and amorphous identification, calibration offset flags, tilt planning and export), and all 8 sampled screens support their nodes. Before filing it needs the CIF-check mode and standard-pattern calibration added (at least as unverified nodes), the pattern-type phases recast as alternatives, and a few general labels corrected.
